column2: the plan wires the linter into `make lint` and pre-commit and requires existing scoped skill markdown to pass or carry justified suppressions, but routes genuine consecutive-bash smells to oos follow-up without requiring inline suppressions. scope covers all `skills/*/skill.md`, `.claude/skills/*/skill.md`, and `skills/*/references/*.md`, yet `### may_update` lists only a subset (e.g. five skill.md files). a first full run finds ~16 adjacent pairs across agnix-fix, audit-runs, combine-issues, release, design, implement, research, and references that are not on that list. filing oos issues alone does not clear lint failures, so the pr can ship with `make lint` red.

the plan assumes one `git_ls_files_z` call covers three disjoint globs (`skills/*/skill.md`, `skills/*/references/*.md`, `.claude/skills/*/skill.md`), but `lint_common.git_ls_files_z` accepts only one pathspec. enumeration as written will not cover all scoped files.

suppression placement conflicts with /implement fence-shape for new-shape fences. `test-implement-fence-shape.sh` rejects fences whose sole nonblank line starts with `#`; a standalone suppression comment line inside `skills/implement/skill.md` launcher fences fails ci even when consecutive-bash lint passes.

indented ```bash openers are not required in the fence parser. scoped files already contain indented bash fences (for example skills/implement/skill.md:199, skills/implement/skill.md:496, skills/research/skill.md:74). sibling linters use leading-whitespace-aware openers (python/lint_literal_counts.py code_fence_regex, scripts/lint-bare-grep-probe.sh awk). if the new parser only matches column-0 fences, those blocks are invisible and adjacency checks can miss or mis-order violations.
